grand_strategy.reading: Nepal is a landlocked hedger between India and China, and its grand strategy has been to get paid for its water and its people while keeping its border claims alive. The September 2025 Gen Z uprising, which brought down Oli and put Sushila Karki in charge of a six-month interim, ended with the March 2026 election, won outright by the Rastriya Swatantra Party (182 of 275 seats) and its prime minister Balendra Shah. The new government has to show that the India-China balance survives its own warmer reset with Delhi and the Lipulekh friction, and that the power and labour economy can carry the state through the next earthquake or flood.

stances.note: Kathmandu cooperates out of necessity (the open border, the 1950 treaty, power and trade that run through India, the Gurkha recruitment) while resisting alignment on the border: the 2020 map and the protests over the India-China Lipulekh trade route (Aug 2025, and again in 2026). No source uses the word 'reluctant' for this pair; the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Trend stable: the Shah government reopened warmly with Delhi (a June 2026 foreign-minister visit reaffirmed cooperation), but the Lipulekh protest of May 2026 stayed. Bond - affinity: open border and shared culture, not kinship; the Kalapani dispute is an open wound, but it is not the structure under the posture.

stances.note: Transactional cooperation with no alignment: Nepal takes Chinese grants and infrastructure talks and does not join anything Beijing leads. The BRI framework of December 2024 was signed, and ten projects were to be expedited, but progress stayed slow: China insists on loans and Nepal accepts grants only (The Diplomat, 2025). Trend stable: the BRI stays mostly at the level of visits and seminars (Kathmandu Post, 2024 and 2026). Bond - none: no kinship, and the Chinese grant of about USD 4m for the 2026 election is aid, not affinity.
